newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat due in Jordan for talks.
newsitem.headline: Arafat due in Jordan for talks.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will fly to Jordan on Monday for talks with Crown Prince Hassan and Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti on the Middle East peace process, officials said.
They said King Hussein, who left hospital on Sunday after minor surgery to his left knee, might join the talks.

It would be the first meeting between Arafat and King Hussein since the Jordanian monarch flew to Gaza and Tel Aviv two weeks ago to help break a deadlock in Palestinian-Israeli talks on the West Bank town of Hebron.
The two sides finally agreed after months of delay on details of an Israeli troop withdrawal from 80 percent of Hebron and a timetable for further redeployment from the West Bank.
Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994.
Its warm ties with the Jewish state cooled after the election of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu last year, while King Hussein's uneasy relations with Arafat seemed to improve.
But Jordan says King Hussein's role in achieving a compromise on Hebron vindicated its policy of maintaining a close dialogue with Israel despite political differences.
